label: copy phase: input f fed back, about to output c (the f->c bigram)
explanation: Fires only in the copy phase, and 97% of the activation mass is on steps where the fed-back input is f. It is strongest when the original sequence had f immediately followed by c, so the model is now outputting c. Top examples are all "x y f c ..." with f at original position 2, which reach about 1.0 of max. In the dev split, f input with c output covers 77% of mass at 0.66 precision. The feature stays silent when that f was the first original token (recall_idx 1), and it never fires in the original or delimiter phases. Weak activations also occur on f inputs followed by other tokens (often f f c or c later in the sequence) and on c inputs before c outputs (about 3% of mass). Those weak cases limit recall.

scorecard.summary: Weighted combination of 40 cues. Raise it: phase=2 & in_tok=f (+7.45), phase=2 & in_tok=c (+5.92), next_out=c (+4.54), in_tok=f (+4.42), phase=2 & out_tok=c (+4.09), out_tok=c (+3.92). Lower it: correct=1 (-5.75), out_tok=g (-2.84), out_tok=m (-2.29), to_go=6 (-2.14).
